role: Same independent primary-source adjudicator continuing on a different narrow question; not an extra fresh vote.
scope: Original English 2008 CE01 / original base 50 / applicable 2018 FAQ. No Technology, variants, Anniversary, expansions, community flare text, or earlier cache used.
case: For an otherwise legally played Machine Wild that applies to the offense’s turn, does its second-encounter guarantee permit a second encounter when the first encounter was unsuccessful?
answer: The guarantee permits the second encounter despite the unsuccessful first encounter. The ordinary first-win-or-successful-deal condition does not remain a condition on this guarantee.
confidence: High within the supplied otherwise-legal-use and applies-to-this-turn conditions.

publication_status.explicit_wording: FAQ p.16 expressly says Machine Wild guarantees the player a second encounter and allows a needed new hand. FAQ p.17 quotes you may always have a second encounter.
publication_status.derived_application: Applying this unqualified guarantee to a first-encounter failure overrides the rulebook’s ordinary success condition. The inspected FAQ does not pose the exact question whether a failed first encounter is covered.
publication_status.not_claimed: No exact named first-failure FAQ pairing, full flare face, full trigger, activation window, role requirement, or all costs is reconstructed.

rules_chain.locator: Original 2008 rulebook p.7, The Turn / Starting the Turn; extraction lines 485–503
rules_chain.published: Ordinarily, a player may have a second encounter only after winning the first or successfully making a deal; the offense normally gets a replacement hand only at turn start.
rules_chain.application: First failure ordinarily ends eligibility. This is the baseline to which the Machine Wild clarification supplies an exception.

rules_chain.locator: Original rulebook p.11, Resolution / After Resolving the Encounter; extraction lines 835–902, especially 876–886 and 898–902
rules_chain.published: If defense won the first encounter, offense has no second encounter; a failed deal likewise gives no second encounter. A first win or successful deal permits a second encounter.
rules_chain.application: Both ordinary losing an attack and ordinary failed-deal cases are covered by the baseline unsuccessful-first condition.

rules_chain.locator: FAQ p.5, second encounter with no encounter cards; extraction lines 430–434; original rulebook p.13 Drawing New Cards, lines 1002–1021
rules_chain.published: Ordinary second-encounter eligibility also requires at least one encounter card left in hand, and the offense normally cannot simply draw a replacement hand later in its turn.
rules_chain.application: This is a separate ordinary barrier. The Machine clarification addresses replacement cards as well as separately stating the encounter guarantee.

rules_chain.published: Machine Wild guarantees the player a second encounter and allows the player to draw a new hand if needed to make that encounter. The answer then explains discarding the old hand, drawing a new one, and returning the flare.
rules_chain.application: The statement guarantees the encounter itself. The phrase if needed qualifies drawing the new hand, not success in the previous encounter. Restricting the guarantee to first success would add a limitation absent from this clarification.

rules_chain.locator: FAQ p.17, continuing Machine entry, extraction lines 1559–1561
rules_chain.published: The question quotes the Wild as you may always have a second encounter; the answer says to play the flare each time its effect is wanted.
rules_chain.application: Always independently corroborates the unqualified second-encounter permission. Per-use activation remains necessary, and is supplied as legal by this case.

rules_chain.locator: Synthesis of the specific Machine Wild FAQ statements and ordinary rulebook eligibility
rules_chain.published: The primary clarification assigns the specific flare effect a guarantee; the ordinary rule describes turns without such a specific effect.
rules_chain.application: When that otherwise legal effect applies to this offense’s turn, ordinary first failure does not negate the very second encounter the effect guarantees. This derives the requested outcome without adding a success limitation or inventing an activation mechanism.

general_exception_context.locator: Original rulebook p.3 Alien Powers and Rules Conflicts, lines 88–92; p.13 Flare Cards, lines 1047–1064.
general_exception_context.published_context: Alien powers can break ordinary rules; flares have their own effects, cannot be played as encounter cards, normally return to hand, and have per-encounter limits.
general_exception_context.limit_on_use: The rulebook precedence sentence expressly addresses alien powers, so it is not misquoted as a universal flare-precedence rule. This decision rests on the specific published Machine Wild guarantee itself. It does not identify Wild with Machine’s alien power or Super.

effect_vs_enabling_conditions.given: Otherwise legal Machine Wild play whose guarantee applies to the offense’s turn.
effect_vs_enabling_conditions.effect_decided: A first failure does not prevent the guaranteed second encounter.
not_inferred: No statement about whether Wild can first be played only after a failure or at any particular phase.
No statement about which roles may initially play it, its complete trigger, or its complete cost.
No assertion that the FAQ’s faceup/draw/return sequence identifies an earliest or latest placement window.
No assertion of more than a second encounter, compulsion to take it, or immunity to unrelated effects.
effect_vs_enabling_conditions.why_condition_is_not_manufacturing_a_mec: The FAQ affirmatively supplies the guarantee and quotes always. The case supplies lawful use and applicability. Deciding the consequence of that effect needs no invented method for making the flare legal. No inspected source contradicts that supplied applicability by imposing a first-success prerequisite on Machine Wild.
effect_vs_enabling_conditions.what_would_need_more_sources: An unconditional table procedure saying exactly when or by whom to activate the flare, particularly an instruction to wait until after a failure and then first play it, requires the full card or a directly applicable timing clarification.

ambiguity_assessment.alternative_reading: The guarantee could merely repair an empty hand while leaving the ordinary first-success rule in force.
ambiguity_assessment.assessment: That reading treats one clause of the FAQ answer as an unstated restriction on its separate guarantee, and cannot account for the quoted always without adding an unprovided success condition. The hand-replacement subject of the FAQ question does not erase its unqualified statement of what Machine Wild guarantees.
ambiguity_assessment.remaining_source_gap: Full activation and role details remain unestablished, but those are outside the supplied conditional effect question. The answer must remain conditional rather than become a complete play instruction.

basis: The assigned primary rulebook explicitly bears a 2008 copyright (lines 1234–1246) and lists 50 alien sheets plus 50 flares (lines 98–115).
The original rulebook supplies the ordinary first/second encounter rules and original flare framework.
The assigned FAQ has an untagged Machine entry directly naming Wild and Super separately, including the Wild guarantee and quoted always wording.
Only the Machine and generic turn/flare material is applied; adjacent expansion entries and Technology/variant rules are not applied.
positive_base_applicability.boundary: Original-base identity is supplied by the assigned corpus and corroborated by these positive contexts; no Anniversary or community full-card reconstruction is used.

procedural_test.bounded_test: Given otherwise legal Machine Wild use applying its guarantee to this turn, does first failure itself disqualify offense from the second encounter?
procedural_test.expected_result: No; the second encounter is permitted despite the first failure.
procedural_test.label: Derived application of an explicit published unqualified guarantee to the ordinary first-success restriction.
procedural_test.not_a_test_of: Role, full trigger, exact first-play timing, complete cost, full card text, or whole flare behavior.
